title: 2k/3 Anyone know how to make a Pseudorandom Number Generator?

posts.author: JimFrom2003
posts.body: I want to use a pseudorandom number generator that generates a seemingly random output from a seed number. Is there any way to do this using RPGM2k3's variable control commands? I want to stress that while the output is seemingly random, the same input number should have the same output every time.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Randomness is only what the player perceives as random.
Therefore tying a variable change function to... Anything without informing the player would create a sense of randomness.
You can base it off steps taken, buttons pushed, events activated, time, or a combination of all of the above.
As far as the seed, yes. I mean it's just a math function. Taking input apply a formula, give output. Take output feed it into the formula, rinse repeat.
You'd likely need to be more specific on what exactly it is you want to achieve.

posts.author: TG22
posts.body:
As a common, reliable, Pseudo-RNG algorithm, you have the Mersenne Twister.
Github is full of implementation of this algorithm in every language.

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body: You can implement some existing algorithm. Maybe a linear congruential generator with some modifications to ensure you stay in the RM2k3 variable range, you probably need some tweaks to avoid the `(a * state) % m` part which would otherwise leave the range, maybe adjusting the algorithm to work with two smaller parts in the calculation. I suggest you ask ChatGPT or some other AI for details here, make sure to state the limitations you are working with (variable range is -9999999 to +9999999 and you have +-*/% operations and conditions and no bitwise operations).

posts.author: Another Fen
posts.body:
If you want to stick with the linear congruential generator idea, Wikipedia also has a good overview and links for possible settings (for example
this paper
)
If you mainly need some smaller values, you could use the example
output = x' = (x * 219) mod 32749
which works within the 9,999,999 limit without the need for emulation (x is your previous RNG output/seed value). It should cycle through 1-32748 in a messy but ultimately repeated order.
Late Edit
: The starting value for x must not be 0
(or a multiple of 32749)
, other values are allowed.
To transform your random output into specific number ranges you can use
number = output mod (max - min + 1) + min
E.g. if you want a number between 30 and 100, you would transform your random output as
number = output mod 71 + 30
For bigger number ranges this will lead to smaller results being a bit more common. If that bothers you then you can reroll output values that are greater than
reroll threshold = 32749 / (max - min + 1) * (max - min + 1)
If you need bigger ranges than 3-4 digits you can also fuse multiple RNG rolls together.
Alternatively, if you also need a longer period, you can probably emulate bigger modulo operations, although at the cost of some performance. (Might be a bit more complex though)
